questions: Why do mobs stop moving far away?
answer: Simulation distance controls how far around players the world actively updates entities and blocks. It can affect farms and mob behavior.

questions: How do I turn off natural mob spawning?
answer: In a world’s settings, disable natural mob spawning. This does not necessarily remove existing mobs or prevent commands and spawn eggs from creating them.
The mob-griefing setting controls certain mob interactions that change blocks or the environment. The affected behaviors vary by mob.

questions: Why is my mob farm not working?
answer: Check difficulty, light levels, spawn-proofing, player distance, and simulation distance. Bedrock spawning ranges and mechanics differ from Java, so use a Bedrock-specific farm design.

questions: Do Java farms always work in Bedrock?
answer: No. Mob spawning, redstone, and some mechanics differ between editions. Use a Bedrock-specific design or verify it in your game version.

questions: Should I turn on experimental features?
answer: Only enable experiments when you understand the risks. Experimental features may change, and worlds using them may behave differently from stable Marketplace-compatible gameplay.
